errors_in_other_reviews: gpt-luna and gpt, claim city-removed-traffic-lanes, verdict 'Not established': this misapplies the brief's decision table rather than misreading a citation. The table reserves Not established for C = 0 with R < T. Both reviewers verified C >= 1: gpt verified three corridors, gpt-luna the 102 Avenue 121-111 Street segment from the May 2017 fact sheet. With C >= 1, only Supported or Partially supported is available. The brief's stakes text defines Partially supported as 'specific removals are established but "all throughout" is not', which is exactly the position both describe. Being unable to compute A is a limitation. It does not put the claim in the C = 0 row.

gpt-luna, claim city-removed-traffic-lanes, citation 132 Avenue Collector Renewal FAQs (https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/132-Avenue-Collector-Renewal-FAQs.pdf?cb=1743727725): overgeneralization, plus a design treated as an outcome. The finding says the avenue was originally two lanes each direction, and 'establishes' removal of a through lane per direction. gpt read the same PDF as saying the former configuration varied. The City's Stage 5 FAQ says a minimum of one lane each way, with two each way only in some sections. The FAQ also describes a design and does not say which segments were built by 2026-09-23. I could not extract the PDF's text (compressed streams), so gpt-luna's two quotes are unverified by me.

gpt-luna, claim city-removed-traffic-lanes, citation 2017 102 Avenue fact sheet: intention treated as outcome. A May 2017 pre-construction sheet that 'lists construction for this segment in 2017' is a plan. gpt-luna cited no completion record. The conclusion survives, because completion is corroborated by the City's November 2017 map (cited by gpt) and by 2017 news reports. The citation alone does not establish it.

gpt, claim city-removed-traffic-lanes, citation Active Transportation Network Expansion page (https://www.edmonton.ca/projects_plans/roads/active-transportation-network-improvements-project), 96 Street 119-124 Avenue: wrong test applied. 'Removal of northbound through movement' (two-way to one-way) is not the brief's criterion. The criterion is a bike lane installed in space that was, or included, a through lane. A City letter to residents reproduced in news coverage, and advocacy reports, say the contraflow lane went in by removing parking on one side. Parking-lane conversions do not count. The segment needs a cross-section drawing before it can count; until then it is provisional. I could not verify the route-table text: HTTP 502 on 2026-09-24.

gpt, claim city-removed-traffic-lanes, citation Active Transportation Network Expansion page, 100 Street 80-83 Avenue: unverified conversion. The project descriptions I could reach, the Strathcona Community League notice (April 2025) and the Ritchie league update, describe a two-way protected lane from 83 to 80 (or 79) Avenue and parking removals. They do not mention a one-way conversion on this segment, and no source I found confirms 'northbound'. The one-way conversions CBC reported in 2018 are on 100 Street north of 83 Avenue, from the Strathcona renewal. Scona likely still qualifies through that earlier segment, but the citation as given does not establish the 80-83 Avenue conversion.

gpt, claim city-removed-traffic-lanes, citation City Council minutes for Charter Bylaw 24001 (https://pub-edmonton.escribemeetings.com/Meeting.aspx?Agenda=PostMinutes&Id=fd2f249c-4d39-4fbf-86ca-8209589f45b3&lang=English): the citation does not support the finding it carries. The placements are probably right (Oliver, Delton and Strathcona/Ritchie), but they are an uncited reviewer inference. The brief requires district areas from the adopted district-plan bylaws.

claims.proposition_evaluated: By 2026-09-23, the City of Edmonton had removed motor-vehicle through lanes and installed bike lanes in that space (or space that included it) on built corridors in at least 8 of the 15 district-plan areas (alternative threshold: 5).
claims.interpretation_notes: Final position: Partially supported. One qualifying corridor is firmly established: 102 Avenue, 121 Street to 112 Street (at least), in Oliver, Central district. The City's May 2017 fact sheet records the westbound through lane removed for a two-way protected bike lane on the north side, with the street converted to one-way eastbound. Completion is corroborated by the City's November 2017 route map, by 2017 news reports of the permanent westbound closure and the 14 November 2017 opening, and by 27 live-layer features on 102 Avenue NW classed 'Protected Bike Lanes - Two Way' (construction_year 2016-2022). So C >= 1 and A >= 1. Two more districts are probable but provisional. North Central: 96 Street, 119-124 Avenue, 2025, two-way to one-way, but the bike lane may sit in former parking space. Scona: 100 Street, from the 2025 80-83 Avenue segment or the earlier Strathcona renewal north of 83 Avenue, per media. 132 Avenue is a fourth candidate. Some sections had two lanes each way, but which of those are among the portions built by the as-of date, and in which district they sit, is not established. Verified minimum: C = 1 and A = 1. Probable: C = 3 and A = 3 (reviewer calculation, provisional). Neither the 8-area nor the 5-area threshold is shown under either count, so both give Partially supported. T and R are not calculated. In the feature unit, 102 Avenue alone contributes 27 live-layer features (not the snapshot). That raises the feature count of C but not A, so the classification does not change. Named examples: (a) 102 Avenue 121-111 Street went from two-way to one-way with a bike lane: occurred, with the 112-111 Street block possibly a parking change only, per the 2015 design sheet. The City's stated reason is to fit the protected bike lane. (b) 102 Avenue east of 109 Street: the one-way single lane east of 107 Street is attributed by the City to Valley Line West LRT. Bike-lane reallocation of former through-lane space is not established. (c) 132 Avenue: the City narrowed sections that had two lanes each way to one lane each way, with separated bike facilities. The contemporaneous reasons are traffic calming and safer speeds, plus the Bike Plan route designation. Built portions are 2024-2025 only; the project is due to finish in 2027. This verdict says nothing about congestion in either direction. Why I do not follow the other two reviewers to Not established: the brief's table reserves that row for C = 0, and all three of us found C >= 1. MATERIAL FRAMING CONCERN: the table has no row for 'C >= 1 and A not determined'. I apply Partially supported on the verified minimum, which the stakes text defines as specific removals established but 'all throughout' not established. A complete census could in principle find A >= 8. Two further concerns. The brief's space test is ambiguous for two-way-to-one-way conversions on local streets, where the bike lane may occupy former parking space: 96 Street and 92 Street turn on this. And the snapshot bytes named in the brief were not in the material I received. Verdict-change record: this package does not reproduce my round-1 verdict, so verdict_changes is empty. Nothing in the other reviews moved me off Partially supported. If my round-1 record shows a different verdict, the reason is the reading of the table above, not the majority view.

claims.suggested_one_line: Edmonton did replace driving lanes with bike lanes on some streets, 102 Avenue in Oliver for certain, but the record shows this in only one to three of 15 districts, not 'all throughout the city'.
claims.suggested_short_answer: City records show that in 2017 Edmonton removed the westbound lane of 102 Avenue between 121 and about 111 Street and put a two-way protected bike lane in its place. Similar conversions are likely in Delton (96 Street, 2025) and Strathcona (100 Street), and parts of 132 Avenue went from two lanes each way to one lane each way. On the evidence found, the conversions fall in one to three of the city's 15 district-plan areas, well short of 'all throughout the city'. The one-lane stretch of 102 Avenue east of 107 Street was done for the LRT. None of this says anything about congestion.
suggested_tldr: Confirmed: 102 Avenue (121 to about 111 Street) lost its westbound lane to a protected bike lane in 2017.
Likely but unconfirmed: Delton's 96 Street, Strathcona's 100 Street, and built parts of 132 Avenue.
One to three of 15 districts on current evidence, so 'all throughout the city' is not established.
This is about what the City built, not what it did to traffic.
